subject.title: feat(cloud-workers): openclaw worker mode running the embedded loop on the box

question: Does the latest worker runtime enforce the intended zero-standing-credentials boundary strongly enough to enable local `exec` and `process` tools on leased machines?
rationale: This introduces a new privileged remote execution boundary, and tests alone cannot establish that the exact launch environment and embedded-agent auth path expose no ambient credentials.

options.title: Require exact-head boundary proof
options.body: Keep the PR open until source review and a redacted live run prove environment scrubbing, worker-only auth handling, machine-clean stdout, and local tool isolation.

options.title: Narrow the initial tool surface
options.body: Land worker composition without credential-sensitive shell tools, then add them after dedicated isolation proof.

options.title: Accept staged milestone risk
options.body: Merge as unreachable infrastructure while requiring the stacked fault-injection gate and a separate enablement review before dispatch becomes available.

recommendation.title: Require exact-head boundary proof
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open until source review and a redacted live run prove environment scrubbing, worker-only auth handling, machine-clean stdout, and local tool isolation.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the merged cloud-worker contract series and the design defining this worker trust boundary.
